title: Chevrolet Caprice Engines by Year (1965–2017)
description: Every factory engine in the Chevrolet Caprice by year: small and big block V8s from 1965, the '80s V6s and diesel, the LT1 B-body and the 2011–17 police Caprice.
intro: The Caprice began as a 1965 luxury package on the Impala Sport Sedan and became Chevrolet's top full-size car through 1996; the 1994–1996 Impala SS has its own page. The name returned from 2011 to 2017 on a police-only sedan. Police engines are marked; California-only engines are noted.
Pick a year to see every engine offered that model year, with its code, rated horsepower and the trims it came in. Each engine links to its full specs.
Small and big block V8s, from the 283 and 327 to the 396, 427 and 454.
The 350, 400, 402 and 454; ratings are SAE net from 1972.

generations.name: 1977–1990 (downsized)
intro: The 250 six and V6s, the 267, 305 and 350 V8s, the Olds 350 diesel and 307, and the 4.3 V6.
The 305 and 350, then the 4.3 L99 and the LT1, including the 9C1 police package.

generations.name: Caprice PPV (2011–2017, police only)
intro: The 6.0 L77 V8 and, from 2012, the 3.6 V6.

sources.name: GM Heritage Center 1965 Chevrolet information kit (full-size line)

excluded.researchNote: Only GM's full-size power-team list (with the Z18 'V-8 only' rule) implies it; Hagerty's Caprice configurations omit L77 (it lists L77 for Impala base/SS). Existence in a Caprice unconfirmed.

excluded.name: 427 V8
excluded.researchNote: NHRA lists 427/425 for 1967 Caprice, but Wikipedia says the 425-hp 427 'was no longer listed' for 1967, GM's 1967 engine data page omits it and Hagerty's 1967 Caprice configurations omit it. Existence doubtful.

excluded.name: 427 V8
excluded.researchNote: Only NHRA lists 427/425 for the 1969 Caprice; Wikipedia's 1969 Caprice text names only the 335/390 427s; not on GM's Sept 1968 page. The L72 is documented for 1969 full-size Chevrolets generally (Impala), not specifically the Caprice.

excluded.name: 350 V8
excluded.researchNote: NHRA lists 350/270 for the 1971 Caprice. GM's Jan 1971 full-size power-team chart lists 350 only as the 245-hp base V8 'except Caprice' and no 270-hp 350; Wikipedia's Caprice engine list has no 350 for 1971. Not confirmed for Caprice.

excluded.name: 3.8L / 231 V6
excluded.researchNote: NHRA's 1979 Caprice Classic rows list 231/115 and 250/115 with their family codes swapped; GM's 1979 power trains and Wikipedia list no V6 before 1980. Treat as NHRA error.

excluded.name: 5.7L / 350 V8
excluded.researchNote: NHRA lists 350/175 for the 1982 Caprice Classic; GM's 1982 Caprice kit lists no gasoline 350. Likely the Impala 9C1 police LM1 (police package was on Impala until 1985). Not a Caprice retail engine.

excluded.name: 2.8L / 173 V6
excluded.researchNote: NHRA lists 173 ci/130 hp for 1985 Caprice Classic; GM's 1985 Caprice kit and EPA show no 2.8 V6 (130 hp is the 4.3 rating). NHRA error; do not list.

method: Every engine and year listed here was confirmed by at least three independent sources: the NHRA Stock Car Classification Guides, factory material such as GM Heritage Center information kits and sales brochures, EPA records and established references. Several Wikipedia articles count as one source. Where sources give different ratings, the factory figure is shown and the difference is noted. Factory race-only packages need two sources.
